pr_title: Handle width and height placeholders in the thumbnail URL
pr_body:
<!--

## Proposed change
The Twitch API does not work with the placeholders `{width`} and `{height}` still present in the URL. 
The API accepts both values set as empty strings, and interprets this as a request for the maximum resolution image. Therefore we modify `".../username-{width}x{height}.jpg"` into `".../username-x.jpg"`, in order to avoid an error.

issue_context.title: Twitch Integration sensor attribute "entity_picture" URL incorrect when channel is Live
issue_context.body:
### The problem

When a channel is offline it provides a working URL to the channel logo in the "entity_picture" attribute.
eg: https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/jtv_user_pictures/uniqueidentifier-profile_image-300x300.png

When a channel is Live, the URL reported is incorrect, which causes anything referencing the attribute to break or show an image error.
Currently when a channel is Live a URL will show as:
entity_picture: https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/previews-ttv/live_user_username-{width}x{height}.jpg

"{width}x{height}.jpg" being the issue.

(Might be worth noting that this is a capture from the live stream and not the channel logo image)

This has been an issue for quite some time.
How long, I am unsure.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.12.2

_No response_

Home Assistant OS

review_comments:
I'm not convinced this will do what you are looking for.

`.format()` on a string will replace variables.
So if the thumbnail_url was
`https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/previews-ttv/live_user_username-{width}x{height}.jpg`
with this change, it would become
`https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/previews-ttv/live_user_username-x.jpg`

Is that what you wanted?

The old code tries to delete the suffix, and should turn
`https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/previews-ttv/live_user_username-{width}x{height}.jpg`
into
`https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/previews-ttv/live_user_username.jpg`

Are you able to find out why the existing code is not working?

The twitch API reference says

>thumbnail_url - A URL to an image of a frame from the last 5 minutes of the stream. Replace the width and height placeholders in the URL ({width}x{height}) with the size of the image you want, in pixels.

True ,Setting the placeholders blank will return 
`https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/previews-ttv/live_user_username-x.jpg`

but this will still retrieve the best stream quality thumbnail available.

The change  from `.replace` to `.format` is just preference, i think its a better way.

However, I do think a resolution should be specified eg...
`stream.thumbnail_url.format(width=640, height=360)`
to reduce bandwidth a loading times.

Maybe in a future update a user preference config option could be added for resolution setting.

Hi @Makrit, thanks for following up.

`.replace` will swap the whole matched string for "", giving you:
`https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/previews-ttv/live_user_username.jpg`

`.format` will replace individual `{width}`, `{height}` variables in the string giving you:
`https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/previews-ttv/live_user_username-x.jpg`
(which would surprise me if it worked, but maybe it does).

I am not clear what you are trying to achieve with the PR, if it is to strip out everything after the name and replace it with `-x`, then I think the existing code is already doing very similar to that.

If the current output still includes the placeholders e.g.
`https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/previews-ttv/live_user_username-{width}x{height}.jpg`
...then the existing code is not running for some reason. **Do you know why?** (It also means that your new code won't run.)

If you are proposing that we should specify width/height, and that the default should be `width=""`, `height=""`, with those values possibly being configurable in the future, I suggest defining the default w/h as constants at the top of the file.

Some pytests would help clarify the intent as well as checking that it works.

Hi @davet2001 
I made the `.replace` change but then edited the PR code for `.format`.

The existing code does not specify any dimensions and therefore returns:
`https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/previews-ttv/live_user_username-{width}x{height}.jpg`

with the "{width}x{height}" unspecified within the image URL path, which does not display an image at all.

That this works is probably edge case on Twitch side, 
`https://static-cdn.jtvnw.net/previews-ttv/live_user_username-x.jpg`

which makes sense as Twitch API requires dimensions to be set, but that's me guessing. Although i do believe dimensions should be set, which makes this irrelevant, I'm just unsure on what would be an acceptable resolution. (My preference is highest as i display big images within lovelace)

I'm suggesting that in a future update, a user preference setting could be added. That's not something i wish to do right now as my only goal here is to fix a bug and not to implement new features.

Ok, I see what you are doing now. Sorry, I was looking at the 2nd commit only, not the full diff.

Please could you update the description of the PR? If I have understood correctly I think it should be something like:

"The Twitch API does not work with the placeholders {width} and {height} still present in the URL. The API accepts both values set as empty strings, and interprets this as a request for the maximum resolution image. Therefore we modify ".../username-{width}x{height}.jpg" into ".../username-x.jpg", in order to avoid an error.

In future we may allow width & height to be specified via configuration parameters. The code is updated to reflect this intent even though there is no way of configuring it yet."

Ah yes, that is my fault, sorry. It's been a while since using github.
Yes that is exactly right, and i am going to copy/paste it because it reads better than mine,
Thanks
